public_rationale: The February 3, 2026 International AI Safety Report describes fabricated information, flawed code, and misleading advice, and says autonomous agents make intervention before harm harder [e1]. It finds that current techniques reduce failure rates but do not reach the reliability required in many high-stakes settings [e1]. This supports the claim as a concern about relying on generative AI for consequential autonomous decisions [e1].
limitations: The report does not establish that every model is unreliable for every task or that supervised applications lack value [e1].
It does not assess a particular military deployment against a specified acceptable error rate [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI systems cannot be trusted.

statement.excerpt: Item 2: These systems cannot be trusted.

from_speaker: weapon systems without humans in the loop
our_interpretation: In context, the ordinary reading concerns depending on generative AI to avoid serious errors in consequential decisions without human verification.
It does not mean that every output is wrong or that no supervised application is useful.
Use February 1–25, 2026 as the latest pre-post assessment window for the ongoing state of the technology; the speaker supplies no reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: Relevant evaluations or a credible synthesis establish persistent material errors and insufficient reliability for consequential autonomous use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative validation establishes dependable performance across the consequential autonomous uses described, with serious errors controlled to applicable safety requirements.
